verify_method: Phase 1 live pass via Exa against primary sources; Phase 2 efficacy enrichment via Consensus. Second pass (2026-07-03) closed the VERIFY/PULL gaps on T-01, T-03, T-04, T-06. Statuses reflect what could be confirmed — honest by design.

claims.claim: Landmark prevalence research on Nebraska's commercial sex market found that roughly 900 individuals are advertised for sex online in the state each month, often multiple times; about 75% show indicators of potential trafficking and 15% are at high risk of being trafficked.
claims.source: Creighton University Human Trafficking Initiative (Price & Clark), Nebraska's Commercial Sex Market (2017), funded by the Women's Fund of Omaha / Sherwood Foundation.
claims.expiry: Vintage-limited: rests on 2017-era Backpage data; Backpage was seized in April 2018. No post-Backpage update from HTI Labs surfaced — treat as historical baseline.
red_team_flags: CORRECTED: the original corpus said '75% of those trafficked are Nebraskans' — that misstated the source. The primary report's ~75% figure means ~75% show INDICATORS of potential trafficking (report states 70-75%). Claim fixed.
The ~900/month figure is from the primary 2017 report; a later Creighton interview rounded it to ~800. 900 matches the published report and the Women's Fund campaign.

Vintage: 2017-era Backpage data (pre-seizure). Frame explicitly as 'landmark prevalence research,' or pair with current NCMEC national trend data (T-02/T-04) rather than presenting as a current count.

claims.claim: NCMEC's CyberTipline received more than 546,000 reports of online enticement in 2024 — roughly a 192% increase over 2023 and a twelve-fold increase since 2021.
claims.source: NCMEC CyberTipline 2024 Data Report; corroborated in U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee testimony (2025).
claims.expiry: NCMEC releases annual CyberTipline data each spring; refresh with the full-year 2025 report.
red_team_flags: Cross-source variance: NCMEC testimony variously cites a 192% and a 194% increase over 2023 (~186,000 reports). 'Roughly 192%' is safe.
This is reporting volume (driven partly by REPORT Act mandates), not a direct prevalence measure — say so.

efficacy_evidence.title: Building the Evidence on Preventing Youth Commercial Sexual Exploitation: Evaluation of the Not a Number Trafficking Prevention Program
efficacy_evidence.cite: Jones et al., 2025, Journal of Interpersonal Violence
efficacy_evidence.finding: Quasi-experimental evaluation found a youth trafficking-prevention education program increased CSE awareness and help-seeking self-efficacy.

claims.claim: NCMEC received nearly 100 reports of financial sextortion per day in 2024, rising to an average of 137 per day in 2025; the victims are predominantly teenage boys, and at least three dozen (36) teenagers in the U.S. have died by suicide since 2021 after being targeted.
claims.source: NCMEC, New Sextortion Data (June 25, 2026) and 2024 in Numbers; FBI/HSI sextortion advisories; corroborated by FinCEN (2025).
claims.expiry: Refresh annually with NCMEC's June sextortion data release.
red_team_flags: The '36' figure is 'at least 36' and counts teenagers (predominantly boys), not exclusively boys — phrasing corrected. FBI counted at least 20 minor suicides Oct 2021–Mar 2023; NCMEC's cumulative 'at least three dozen since 2021' is the current figure. Both are floors, not totals.
Rate note: ~100/day is the 2024 figure (36,000+ reports); 137/day is 2025 (50,000+ reports). Cite the year you mean.

claims.claim: In the first half of 2025, NCMEC CyberTipline reports of online enticement rose 77% year over year (from 292,951 to 518,720) and child sex trafficking reports surged from 5,976 to 62,891, following the REPORT Act's expanded mandatory reporting.
claims.source: NCMEC, 'Spike in Online Crimes Against Children a Wake-Up Call' — first-ever mid-year (Jan–Jun) CyberTipline data (Sept 2025); corroborated in U.S. Senate Judiciary testimony (Dec 2025).
claims.expiry: Mid-year figure; supersede with NCMEC full-year 2025 report (the CyberTipline data page already cites full-year 2025: +158% enticement, +323% CST vs 2024).
red_team_flags: Attribution: the child-sex-trafficking surge is largely a reporting-mandate artifact — the REPORT Act newly required ESPs to report CST and online enticement (a ~952% H1-over-H1 jump). This exposes existing volume, not a sudden rise in offenses. State this explicitly.

claims.claim: Generative-AI-related child exploitation reports to NCMEC increased 1,325% in 2024 (to more than 67,000), and escalated further to 440,419 in the first half of 2025 — a fast-emerging threat category for prevention education.
claims.source: NCMEC, 2024 in Numbers; U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee testimony of L. Coffren, NCMEC (Dec 9, 2025).
claims.expiry: Fast-moving; the H1 2025 figure (440,419) will be superseded by full-year 2025 data.
red_team_flags: The H1 2025 spike is partly attributable to a handful of AI companies newly implementing detection/reporting — a reporting artifact as well as a real trend. Note both.

efficacy_evidence.title: A Systematic Review of the Education and Awareness Interventions to Prevent Online Child Sexual Abuse
efficacy_evidence.cite: Patterson et al., 2022, Journal of Child & Adolescent Trauma
efficacy_evidence.finding: Education/awareness interventions improved online-safety knowledge, though effects on risky online behavior were limited — supports prevention education while flagging its known limits.

efficacy_evidence.title: Building the Evidence on Preventing Youth Commercial Sexual Exploitation: Not a Number Program Evaluation
efficacy_evidence.cite: Jones et al., 2025, Journal of Interpersonal Violence
efficacy_evidence.finding: Youth trafficking-prevention education increased CSE awareness and help-seeking self-efficacy in a quasi-experimental high-school trial.

claims.claim: In 2024 the National Human Trafficking Hotline identified 71 trafficking cases in Nebraska (from 148 signals) and 88 cases in Iowa (from 166 signals); since 2007 it has identified 621 cases in Nebraska and 873 in Iowa.
claims.source: National Human Trafficking Hotline, Statistics by State (2024; all-time since 2007), retrieved data current as of April 2025.
claims.expiry: Hotline updates annually; the operation transitioned from Polaris to Compass Connections in late 2025 — watch for methodology changes.
red_team_flags: Hotline counts measure reporting/contact volume from those who chose to contact the Hotline, NOT prevalence — the Hotline itself states this. Frame as 'identified cases,' never as the true number of victims.
